title: Oklahoma oil-rich Indians and an oilman who pitched Cab Calloway
summary: Thomas tells of a woman whose land produced a million barrels a day and a part-Indian oilman who tried to sell Cab stock in Longview, Texas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We had one girl in Oklahoma (I think she was from around Muskogee, too), and the land they gave her... At one time her oil wells were producing a million barrels of oil a day. Now, see, when they gave up that land, they didn't know the oil was there. I mean, they found this oil!

And there was another family I knew; his father was part-Indian. So when they needed some money, he made them buy the land from him. And he always said by the time he passed on they'd know how to take care of it -- because he was going to give it back to them when he passed on. And this guy, he met us in Texas... I don't know whether you were with the band or not. He met us in Texas, and tried to talk Cab into some stock on all that oil they found down there in Texas. He was involved with that.

Yeah, Longview. And he tried to sell Cab some stock. But Cab didn't have... He didn't know what the oil was. But he was into oil, and he knew about it. He went to study... His son wound up being a vice-president over here in New Jersey at Standard Oil. And he... He went to school...I understand... I don't know whether this story is accurate or not. But he went to school with one of the African fellows, where they found that oil in Africa, and it was through him that the United States got the deal. He did it on account of him being a classmate of his.

And I don't know... I went to visit him down there, and he took me to a... They got a building in Tulsa called the Oil Building, and he's a member, and he took me up there, and they had entertainment and everything. And my sister went to school with his wife. See, that's how they were so friendly.
